subject: MedX Hosting & Residency — air-gap / VPC constraints (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@medxhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: MedX hosting constraints & next steps (air-gap / VPC)

Alex — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment after the call. Please reply to confirm or correct anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulator-driven requirement to keep PHI on-prem or in a customer-managed VPC within a dedicated cloud tenancy.
- Strict egress controls and no outbound internet from the inference cluster (air-gap style).
- Need for audit logs/KMS-managed keys and retention for 7+ years for certain datasets.
- Predictable latency SLOs for clinician-facing flows (95th percentile < 300ms) while preserving cost targets.

Goals from your side:
1) Validate a private deployment architecture that satisfies audit/evidence requirements.
2) Confirm networking constraints and whether controlled egress to Redwood control plane is acceptable via a proxy or if fully air-gapped is required.
3) Get a list of required deliverables for procurement/security review (network diagrams, SOC2 evidence).

Action items we agreed on:
- Redwood: produce a high-level private deployment diagram showing VPC peering options, proxy-based control-plane access, and an isolated-airgap alternative (deliver by 2028-05-15).
- MedX: confirm whether outbound-only HTTPS via an approved proxy is permitted (Natasha to respond by COB 2028-05-14).
- Both: schedule a follow-up technical deep-dive with MedX infra/security (30–45 minutes) the week of 2028-05-20.

Attachments: medx-network-zone-map.pdf (placeholder) — initial sketch we'll refine. Also attaching completed SOC2 questionnaire (SOC2-questionnaire-completed.xlsx) for your security team to review.

If this looks good, I'll lock the follow-up on your calendar and include our Solutions Engineer for the tech deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@medxhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Natasha Li <natasha.li@medxhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: MedX hosting constraints & next steps (air-gap / VPC)

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side:  

- We're a US-based provider with state-level regulations that mandate customer-controlled key management for certain PHI workloads. That makes KMS/HSM integration a hard requirement for those datasets.
- For initial scope, the secure inference (clinician workflows) must be in a VPC under our account; we prefer no general internet egress from those instances.
- We are open to an outbound-only, tightly controlled proxy for metrics and health-checks, but security wants to evaluate that option — it's not a given.

Natasha will pull together the specific network ACLs and the procurement list (including any approval forms). We'll aim to have that to you by EOD 2028-05-14.

Also: can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for Private deployments? If yes, what proof/evidence do you provide?

Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Security | MedX Health
alex.mercer@medxhealth.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Prep for MedX infra deep-dive

Karthik / Laura — re: Alex's questions, quick notes to prepare before the tech call:  

- KMS: Redwood Private supports CMK integration via customer KMS (we have integrations for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM gateways). For the deck, include our KMS architecture diagram and a short matrix of supported key operations (encrypt/decrypt/sign?). Add extractable evidence items: key rotation logs, CMK policy examples, and an audit log sample.
- Network options: outline three architectures — (A) VPC peering + restricted egress via NAT/proxy; (B) Private control plane via private link + outbound proxy for telemetry; (C) Fully air-gapped with manual model sync and on-prem operator. Indicate pros/cons and compliance fit.
- Latency: note that continuous batching and local KV caching can help meet 95p < 300ms; however, we should capture the expected token rates for clinician flows to size nodes.

I'll take the KMS evidence items and draft the architecture slide. Laura, can you pull a short latency primer and the model-sync playbook?

Thanks — I want the follow-up to be hands-on, not theoretical.

-Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
From: Natasha Li <natasha.li@medxhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@medxhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: MedX hosting constraints & next steps (air-gap / VPC)

All — quick confirmation from Security/Network:  

- We will provide the network ACLs and approved proxy configuration by 2028-05-14 COB.
- For initial PoC, MedX security will accept an outbound-only HTTPS proxy to a whitelisted Redwood control-plane IP range, provided we receive the SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration plan.
- For long-term, security prefers a fully isolated deployment pattern, but acknowledges a proxy-based model may be acceptable for a tightly-scoped pilot.

Next steps (as we see them):
1) Redwood to share a two-slide summary (KMS evidence + network options) by 2028-05-15.
2) Schedule a deep-dive: propose 2028-05-22 10:00–10:45 PT — will that work for Redwood?
3) We'll circulate procurement checklist and required forms alongside the network ACLs.

Natasha Li
Senior Network Security Engineer | MedX Health
natasha.li@medxhealth.com
